concepts.title: Food Gathering and Hunting
concepts.definition: The earliest primary activities are food gathering and hunting, practised today by small groups like the Bushmen of Kalahari, Pygmies of Congo and the Chukchis, whose tools are simple and whose survival depends on the natural availability of plants and animals.
concepts.key_idea: These economies neither cultivate nor herd: they live directly on what nature offers, which keeps them mobile and small in number.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy104.txt food gathering and hunting sections with tribal examples
question_patterns: name present-day hunter-gatherer groups and their regions
why are hunting-gathering economies always small in numbers
what tools characterise gatherer-hunter groups
how does mobility suit a gathering economy
compare hunting with gathering as livelihoods
why is this activity called a primary activity

solution_steps.explain: Bushmen, Pygmies and Chukchis are the chapter's surviving examples
dependence on wild produce caps population density and forces movement
extracting food directly from nature makes it primary in the strictest sense

concepts.title: Pastoral Nomadism and Transhumance
concepts.definition: Pastoral nomadism is a subsistence herding system in which nomads move with camels, yaks, sheep and goats across arid lands of Sahara, Central Asia and Tibet following fodder; in mountain regions like the Alps the seasonal movement of herders between high pastures and valleys is called transhumance.
concepts.key_idea: Nomadism is horizontal mobility across drylands while transhumance is vertical mobility across mountains, both timed by seasons.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy104.txt pastoral nomadism and transhumance passages
question_patterns: define pastoral nomadism with regions and animals
what is transhumance and where is it practised
distinguish nomadism from transhumance
how do nomads decide their movement routes
why do herdsmen prefer camels and goats in deserts
compare ranching with pastoral nomadism

solution_steps.explain: nomads roam drylands; transhumant herders climb Alps pastures seasonally
camels, goats and sheep survive aridity; yaks suit high altitude cold
both movements follow the calendar of fodder availability

concepts.title: Types of Agriculture
concepts.definition: Agriculture ranges from intensive subsistence farming of dense monsoon Asia, plantation agriculture of tropical estates (tea, coffee, rubber), extensive commercial grain farming of North American prairies, mixed farming and dairy of western Europe, Mediterranean agriculture with viticulture, to co-operative, collective and state farms of the socialist tradition.
concepts.key_idea: Farm types answer market and environment together: subsistence feeds the household, plantations and grain farms feed the world market.
question_patterns: distinguish intensive subsistence from extensive commercial farming
what crops characterise plantation agriculture
define viticulture and its region
how do dairy and mixed farming differ
describe collective and state farms of the former USSR
why is Mediterranean agriculture specialised in horticulture

solution_steps.explain: subsistence types sell little; commercial types organise for the market
tea estates, prairie wheat farms and Danish dairies typify distinct systems
co-operative, collective and state farms differ by who owns and manages them

concepts.title: Mining and Fishing
concepts.definition: Mining extracts minerals through surface or shaft methods, its location fixed by geological occurrence but profitability decided by transport and market factors; fishing, an age-old primary activity, divides into inland and deep-sea fishing with modern vessels using sonar and freezing technology.
concepts.key_idea: Both activities depend on nature's endowment but their scale is set by technology and demand.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy104.txt mining factors and fishing methods sections
question_patterns: list the physical and economic factors affecting mining
compare surface and shaft mining
distinguish inland from deep-sea fishing
what technologies raised the fish catch in modern times
why is fishing concentrated on continental shelves
relate primary activities to resource depletion risks

solution_steps.explain: geology decides where minerals lie; economics decides whether mining pays
shallow warm shelves teem with plankton and so with fish
sonar, refrigeration and factory ships industrialised the catch

worked_examples.question_pattern: Differentiate pastoral nomadism from transhumance with regions.

solution_template.explain: dryland herders of Sahara and Central Asia move long distances for fodder
Alpine herders shift vertically between valley winter homes and summer pastures
the first is wide horizontal roaming, the second a fixed seasonal climb

worked_examples.question_pattern: Classify prairie grain farming, Assam tea estates and Danish dairy farming into the chapter's farm types.

solution_template.explain: extensive commercial grain farming with machinery and export orientation
plantation agriculture with hired labour and a single crop
dairy farming linked to mixed farming and market cooperatives

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain why a rich mineral deposit may still remain unexploited.

solution_template.explain: deposits occur where nature put them, not where demand is
distance from market and transport costs can erase profits
exploitation waits until price and infrastructure turn the deposit viable
